In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the H-score is a good indicator of how much a task transfer learning problem is going to benefit from a transfer learning algorithm.
H-score can provide a good measure of transferability in task transfer learning, which is easy to compute and generalizes to different types of inference problems.

H-score provides an information-theoretic metric of transferability for task transfer learning, which has a direct connection between the asymptotic error rate and the transferability of the representations, and can be applied to various transfer learning settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a novel information theoretic formulation of transferability, which can be used to select source tasks and design efficient transfer learning policies, and can generalize to inference tasks beyond classification.
we present an information-theoretic formulation of transferability that is easy to compute and generalizes to a variety of tasks and domains.
we present a principled information-theoretic formulation for transferability in task transfer learning and provide an easy to compute metric that is useful for both task and feature selection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transferability between tasks can be estimated in a principled and computable manner.
transferability can be quantified in terms of the amount of mutual information shared by source and target tasks and this metric can be used to guide transfer learning algorithms.
a principled information-theoretic approach is effective in quantifying transferability and can be used to devise efficient transfer-learning policies.
